part.text:
Fixed. The issue was that multi-thread runtime worker threads are spawned through the blocking pool (`Launch::launch` uses `runtime::spawn_blocking` in tokio/src/runtime/scheduler/multi_thread/worker.rs:447), so `num_blocking_threads()` counted them.

Fix (matching upstream tokio#6551): subtract the worker count in both schedulers:

- tokio/src/runtime/scheduler/multi_thread/handle/metrics.rs:10 — `num_threads().saturating_sub(self.num_workers())`
- tokio/src/runtime/scheduler/multi_thread_alt/handle/metrics.rs:10 — same

Verification: `cargo test -p tokio --test rt_metrics --features full` with `--cfg tokio_unstable` now passes all 20 runnable tests including `num_blocking_threads`, `num_idle_blocking_threads`, and `num_workers`; the only failures are the two network-dependent `io_driver_*` tests (no internet in the container), which are unrelated to this change.
